subject: Post-call follow-up: model-fit deep dive, benchmarks, and A/B runbook
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Johnson <sara.johnson@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call follow-up: model-fit deep dive, benchmarks, and A/B runbook

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways
- BrightCart wants a rerank-first flow for search results (primary) and category recommendations (secondary).
- Main success metrics: NDCG@10 and MRR for facet-driven queries, plus manual QA on topical freshness.
- Constraint: tail latency SLO of 150ms p95 for queries during peak; infra lead will confirm ideal batch sizes.

Deliverables we committed to:
1) A short model-fit packet: recommended candidate models, quantization profile options, and expected latency/cost tradeoffs. (See link below.)
2) Benchmark results on your sample prompt set and our internal prompt variations (NDCG/MRR table).
3) A draft A/B runbook for an initial canary (50k impressions/day) including rollback criteria and monitoring signals.

Immediate ask for you: can you confirm the canonical prompt set (or share the latest export) and the target traffic slice for the pilot (search only vs search+recommendations)?

Links and artifacts attached: brightcart_promptset_v2.jsonl (sample + annotations), preliminary ndcg_mrr_summary_q3.xlsx, and an A/B runbook draft.

Proposed timeline
- Sep 8: Marcus to share preliminary NDCG/MRR from our internal dry run.
- Sep 9: Sync to review numbers + finalize canary thresholds.
- Sep 14: Target canary start (pending procurement + infra).

If that works, I’ll loop in Sergio from the Sales Engineering team for procurement and billing questions.

Thanks — feel free to reply with any clarifications.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

We attached our latest export to this reply (search_prompts_final_20260907.jsonl) — it’s the landing set we want to use for the pilot (focused on search, ~120k unique queries/day). For the pilot we’d like to start with search only.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: model-fit deep dive, benchmarks, and A/B runbook

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 3:12 PM Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Key takeaways

Hi all — I ran the BrightCart prompt export through three candidate rerank configurations on a small staging pool (1xA10g) to get preliminary signals. High-level numbers (aggregated across the 12k-sample subset):

- Candidate A (open-variant-1, FP16): NDCG@10 = 0.612, MRR = 0.457, p95 latency = 128ms
- Candidate B (open-variant-2 + post-filter): NDCG@10 = 0.638, MRR = 0.471, p95 latency = 165ms
- Candidate C (redwood-rerank-qtz8): NDCG@10 = 0.629, MRR = 0.463, p95 latency = 142ms

Preliminary take: Candidate B gives the best retrieval quality but exceeds your p95 SLO at current staging batch sizes. Candidate A meets the SLO and is lowest cost; Candidate C is a middle ground and has a quantized path we can optimize.

Proposed A/B plan (short):
- Canary cohort: 10% traffic for 7 days; holdout = current baseline (your existing ranker).
- Metric primary: delta NDCG@10 (target uplift >= +3.5% relative) and delta MRR (>= +2%).
- Safety signals: latency p95, error rate, manual QA failure rate. Any breach triggers immediate rollback plus 1:1 incident review.

I’ll prepare a full spreadsheet with the per-query slice results and suggested thresholds by query bucket by EOD Sep 8.

-Marcus
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: ndcg_mrr_summary_q3.xlsx (34KB)

On Wed, Sep 8, 2026 at 9:32 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed A/B plan (short):

Quick note from the Ops/Canary side:
- We need to add regression detection hooks to the runbook before canary start. Specifically: topical drift alerts (embedding-based divergence), long-tail token hallucination checks (sampled QA), and a daily human review on the 200 query sample Sara requested.
- For Candidate B, if we want to hit the p95 latency SLO we can test a smaller micro-batch path plus KV cache warmup; I’ll work with infra on a staged optimization plan.
- Security/compliance: if BrightCart wants document-level PII redaction we should list that as a blocker for ramp >25% (requires a short privacy review).

I’ll draft the runbook with explicit rollback run steps and monitoring dashboards by Sep 9 morning.

Laura Bennett
Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: model-fit deep dive, benchmarks, and A/B runbook

Thanks everyone — great progress. Quick summary & asks from me so procurement and scheduling can proceed: 

Summary of recommended next steps
- Use Candidate C as the initial production candidate for a conservative canary after Marcus’s full per-query analysis (Candidate C balances quality and latency with straightforward quantization optimizations).
- Canary plan: 10% traffic, 7 days, with daily manual QA (200-sample) and automatic rollback on latency p95 > 160ms or NDCG drop below baseline.
- Add a pre-ramp privacy check for PII redaction if BrightCart expects ramp >25%.

Action items
- Sara: confirm procurement timeline and introduce procurement lead to Sergio (ASAP).
- Marcus: share per-query spreadsheet and final thresholds (EOD Sep 8).
- Laura: finalize ab_runbook_draft.md with monitoring dashboards and regression hooks (by Sep 9 morning).
- Sergio: I’ll need contract schedule and PO details for a Sep 21 billing start (tentative).

We’ll plan a short sync on Sep 9 to finalize thresholds — I’ll send a calendar invite once Sara confirms procurement contact.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the canary live.

Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
